name: Telescope Array
summary: A Utah cosmic-ray observatory uses a large scintillator surface array and fluorescence telescopes. Its surface data also support dedicated searches for ultra-high-energy neutrinos.
physics_targets: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and multimessenger constraints
detection_principle: Scintillator stations sample charged particles and shower-front timing. Multivariate classifiers distinguish deeply developing neutrino showers from the dominant proton and nuclear cosmic-ray background.

status.label: Operating / data taking
status.evidence: An operating cosmic-ray observatory with a published dedicated neutrino analysis.

timeline.event: TA×4 expands the cosmic-ray array; it is an observatory phase rather than a separate neutrino discovery.

collaboration.name: Telescope Array Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Station spacing
key_parameters.value: Approximately 1.2 km in the original array

key_parameters.name: Neutrino dataset
key_parameters.value: Nine years, 2008–2017, in the cited search

key_parameters.name: Discrimination
key_parameters.value: Sixteen shower-front and lateral-distribution observables in the published classifier

results.summary: Reported an upper bound on the ultra-high-energy down-going neutrino flux above 10¹⁸ eV. The result is a neutrino limit, not a detected neutrino population.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
